questions.question: You plan to deploy Azure Bastion to VNet1. Which subnet configuration should you create?

options.text: A subnet named AzureBastionSubnet with a /26 prefix
options.why: Correct. Bastion requires this exact name and a /26 or larger subnet.

options.text: A subnet named BastionSubnet with a /27 prefix
options.why: The name must be AzureBastionSubnet, and /27 is too small.

options.text: A subnet named GatewaySubnet with a /26 prefix
options.why: GatewaySubnet is used for VPN and ExpressRoute gateways.

options.text: A subnet named AzureBastionSubnet with a /29 prefix
options.why: A /29 is smaller than the required /26.

questions.explanation: Azure Bastion is deployed to a dedicated subnet named AzureBastionSubnet with a prefix of /26 or larger.

questions.question: Administrators must connect to Azure VMs by using the native SSH client on their workstations through Azure Bastion. Which Bastion configuration meets the requirement?

options.text: Standard SKU with native client support enabled
options.why: Correct. Native client connections require Standard or Premium with native client support.

options.text: Basic SKU with a Standard public IP address
options.why: The Basic SKU supports connections from the Azure portal only.

options.text: Developer SKU
options.why: The Developer SKU supports portal connections to one VM at a time.

options.text: Basic SKU with IP-based connection
options.why: IP-based connection requires the Standard SKU, and it does not enable the native client.

questions.explanation: The az network bastion ssh and az network bastion rdp commands require the Standard or Premium SKU with native client support (tunneling) enabled.

questions.question: Azure Bastion is deployed in a hub virtual network. VM1 is in a spoke virtual network that is peered with the hub. VM1 has no public IP address. Can administrators use the Bastion host to connect to VM1?

options.text: Yes, because Bastion can connect to VMs in peered virtual networks
options.why: Correct. Bastion connects to the private IP address of VMs in peered virtual networks.

options.text: No, because VM1 requires a public IP address
options.why: Bastion connects to private IP addresses, so a public IP is not required.

options.text: No, because Bastion must be deployed in the same virtual network as the VM
options.why: Bastion supports VMs in peered virtual networks.

options.text: Yes, but only if gateway transit is enabled
options.why: Gateway transit is not required for Bastion.

questions.explanation: One Bastion host in a hub can serve VMs in peered spokes when the peerings are connected and NSGs allow RDP or SSH from the Bastion subnet.

questions.question: You deploy Azure Bastion. Administrators cannot connect to VM1 through Bastion. The subnet of VM1 has an NSG. Which inbound rule should the NSG include?

options.text: Allow TCP 3389 and 22 from the address range of AzureBastionSubnet
options.why: Correct. Bastion connects to the VM private IP from its own subnet.

options.text: Allow TCP 443 from the Internet service tag
options.why: Administrators connect to Bastion on 443. The VM receives RDP or SSH from Bastion.

options.text: Allow TCP 3389 from the Internet service tag
options.why: This exposes the VM to the internet, which Bastion is meant to avoid.

options.text: Allow all traffic from the AzureLoadBalancer service tag
options.why: This tag is used for load balancer health probes.

questions.explanation: The target VM must accept RDP (3389) or SSH (22) from the Bastion subnet. The default AllowVnetInBound rule also allows it unless a higher-priority rule denies it.

questions.question: Which two features require the Standard or Premium SKU of Azure Bastion? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Host scaling by changing the instance count
options.why: Correct. Basic uses a fixed two instances.

options.text: Shareable links
options.why: Correct. Shareable links are available in Standard and Premium.

options.text: Connecting to a VM from the Azure portal
options.why: All SKUs support portal connections.

options.text: Connecting to VMs in the same virtual network
options.why: All SKUs connect to VMs in the same virtual network.

questions.explanation: Standard adds host scaling, native client support, IP-based connection and shareable links. Premium adds features such as session recording.
